decision.detail: Phil sets the coach bag on the bench beside him. He sits down. Hard, the way you sit when the seat is metal and the floor is tile and the fluorescent tube above hums at sixty hertz. He pulls his coat off, drapes it over his shoulders. He folds his arms on the bench back. He closes his eyes. He does not pick up the phone. He does not walk toward the ballroom. He does not call his sister. He does not call Bedrock. He does not say a word to the terminal clerk who is already gathering his pens and turning the register toward the small hours. He breathes. He lets the hum take him. He will wake at 7:15, maybe 7:30. He will find the payphone or the clerk's phone or the sister's number on a scrap of paper in the coat pocket. He will confirm the van. He will be at the door at 8. The couch will be moved. He does not need the evening to mean anything. He needs the body to be rested and the feet to be on the right side of the street at the right hour. The ballroom lights go out. The line goes quiet. He is in the dark and the hum and the bench and the bag beside him and the coat over his shoulders and the Tuesday in his chest is only a Tuesday and he lets it be only that.
decision.intention: Rest the body. Be at the door at 8. Move the couch. Do not test the shape. Do not play the bars. Do not sit behind the rig. Be the man in the folding chair at the terminal who is going to be at the door at 8. The thing is the thing. The rest is the rest. Nothing else is required of the evening.
